key_insight: Agentic (multi‑agent) AI tools are increasingly popular but must be deployed with clear motivations, explanations, and transparency to avoid wasted computational and human resources in scientific workflows.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap between hype and practical utility for multi‑agent systems by calling for transparency about why agents are used, what they do, and how their outputs and costs are measured—reducing wasted effort, improving reproducibility, and enabling informed adoption.
method: Define and document clear motivations and success criteria before introducing agentic components into a workflow.
Require transparency mechanisms: agent role descriptions, decision logs, provenance/audit trails, and resource/cost accounting.
Integrate human oversight and quantitative evaluations (efficiency, accuracy, reproducibility) to justify agent use vs. simpler alternatives.
impact: Promotes responsible, efficient adoption of multi‑agent AI in research by enabling practitioners to evaluate benefits, control costs, and reproduce results—raising trust and practical value of agentic systems.
visual_elements: Flowchart of a scientific workflow with agentic modules annotated by 'motivation', 'inputs', 'outputs', and 'cost' labels
Bar chart comparing resource/time cost and accuracy for: human-only, single-agent, and multi-agent approaches
Checklist / audit trail graphic showing required transparency items (roles, logs, provenance, metrics)
Icon set for stakeholders (researcher, auditor, compute budget) linked to decision points
